# Drawer

A panel that slides up from the bottom, for phones.

<p class="odv-compstatus"><span class="odv-pill odv-pill-out">Left out of Dense data</span> A drawer is for phones. Dense data's experts work at a desk with a mouse and keyboard, and the scheme avoids first-time visitors on phones. <span class="odv-instead">Use instead: <a href="./sheet">Sheet</a>, <a href="./dialog">Dialog</a></span></p>

## When to use it

- **Use it when:** Filters, details or a short form on a phone, while the page stays partly in view.
- **Not when:** A blocking decision (dialog), or a wide screen where a side panel fits better (sheet).

Instead:

- [Sheet](./sheet.md): Slides from an edge on wide screens.
- [Dialog](./dialog.md): A blocking decision.

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Accessibility and keyboard

| Keyboard | What happens | Not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| undefined | Escape closes it. | undefined |

Test before you ship:

- [ ] It behaves as a dialog: named, focus moves in and back. undefined

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add drawer
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Drawer reads 12 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Drawer's tokens to change Drawer alone.
